generic_sampling_rules.text_identifier: 32-char lowercase hex string; primary keys unique; foreign keys drawn from parent pool; NULL share per column statistics where nullable; no orphan values (FK integrity preserved)
generic_sampling_rules.text_short_enum: sample from the observed value pool for the column; include near-variants (case flip, trailing x, one-char substitution) at 5% of rows
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: sample from observed pool with 10% fresh near-duplicate variants; NULL share per column statistics
generic_sampling_rules.text_long: sample from observed pool; 5% near-duplicate variants; NULL share per column statistics
generic_sampling_rules.real_amount: non-negative REAL rounded to 2 decimals; range from statistics; NULL share per column statistics where nullable
generic_sampling_rules.real_coordinate: REAL in [-180,180] for longitude, [-90,90] for latitude; 20-50% duplicate share
generic_sampling_rules.integer_count: positive INTEGER; 20-50% duplicate share; NULL share per column statistics where nullable
generic_sampling_rules.near_variant: for each listed literal L: include L, L||'x', lower(L), and one-char-substituted variant; for LIKE targets also include L||'%'; apply in both enum and generic sampling branches
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: for each listed literal L: include L, one step below, one step above (numbers by step, dates by one day); for text literals use case variants (L, lower(L), upper(L)); apply in both enum and generic sampling branches
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: each nullable column gets at least one NULL row; share follows column statistics
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_for_distinct: 20-50% of rows share a value with another row; apply after near-variant injection and re-check after NULL planting
generic_sampling_rules.ties_for_order_limit: at least two rows tie at the top ranks of the ORDER column
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join_rows: for each nullable FK: ~5% NULL values only (no orphan values, to preserve declared FK constraints); ensure some parent rows have no children by not referencing them

semantic_rules_and_formulas.formula: poverty_level IN ('highest poverty','high poverty','moderate poverty','low poverty')

generation_specification.uncertainty: FK integrity is preserved: nullable FKs (donations.projectid, resources.projectid, essays.projectid) receive NULL values only, never orphan values, so declared foreign key constraints hold. Parent rows without children are obtained by leaving some projects unreferenced. essays.projectid must be drawn from the projects.projectid pool so essays.teacher_acctid can be copied from the matching project (non-orphan rows get non-NULL teacher_acctid; NULL only where the parent teacher_acctid is NULL). donation_total formula holds only when optional support is included; conditional variant covers the other case. Derived formulas are asserted only for non-NULL operands (SQL three-valued logic); planted NULLs are never replaced. Some enum pools (payment_method, resource_type) may have additional values not shown in the sample. school_metro NULL share 12.2% observed.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 units fail with ValueError('empty range for randrange() (370, 231, -139)'). The traceback originates in NumberSampler.sample() in values.py: `v = self._fresh_or_reuse(lambda: r.randint(int(lo), int(hi)) ...)` where lo/hi come from `(self.list_min, self.list_max)` when not full. In NumberSampler.__init__, `self.list_max = min(self.max, _MAX)` is set to the global max (e.g. 10**scale) rather than the observed list max, while `self.list_min = min(self.elements)`. When the observed minimum (e.g. 370) exceeds the capped global max (e.g. 231), randint(370, 231) raises. This is the documented 'list_max overwrite quirk' but it is not guarded, so generation produces zero instances.
issues.requested_revision: Guard the range in NumberSampler.sample(): if int(lo) > int(hi), swap or fall back to the full range (self.min, self.max), or set list_max = max(list_min, min(self.max, _MAX)). Ensure every unit builds and writes successfully (n_fail == 0) before re-submitting.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_spec_size` computes `lo = max(0, base - 30)`, `hi = min(230, base + 30)` and returns `rng.randint(lo, hi)`. For projects/essays base=200 -> hi=230, lo=170 (ok); for donations/resources base=400 -> hi=min(230,430)=230, lo=370 -> randint(370,230) is an empty range. This is a second, independent source of the same ValueError and also contradicts the specification's table_sizes_per_instance (donations=400, resources=400): the cap of 230 silently shrinks those tables to at most 230 rows.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the hard-coded 230 cap (or make it base-relative, e.g. hi = base + 30) so that donations and resources are generated at ~400 rows as specified, and so lo <= hi always holds.

issues.evidence: writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` with no orig_path, so the branch `if orig_path is None or not os.path.exists(orig_path)` re-creates the schema from DDL and inserts only the generated rows. The specification and the module docstring state generated rows are appended to a copy of the compact database ('The compact rows are never deleted or changed; generated rows are appended'). With orig_path=None the compact rows are not preserved, so the instance is not the compact DB plus generated rows.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the worker args and call write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path=orig)) so the compact rows are copied and preserved, and generated rows are appended.

issues.evidence: instance.build_random_instance calls `_apply_nulls` after `_derive_projects`/`_derive_donations`, but `_derive_projects` sets incl[i] = e + opt only when excl[i] is not None; if `_apply_nulls` later nulls total_price_excluding_optional_support the incl value remains, which is fine, but the reverse (nulling incl) leaves excl set — acceptable under three-valued logic. However `_derive_donations` writes `total[i]` for every i including rows where `donation_total` will subsequently be nulled by `_apply_nulls`; that is consistent with 'planted NULL never replaced'. The real gap: `_apply_nulls` is applied to `donation_total` (share 0.10) but the formula `donation_total = donation_to_project + donation_optional_support` is only enforced for non-NULL operands, which is satisfied. No blocking issue here, but note `_derive_essays` sets teacher_acctid from the project map and then `_apply_nulls` may null it — consistent. Flagging only that `_derive_projects` does not enforce `total_price_including_optional_support >= total_price_excluding_optional_support` when excl is NULL but incl is non-NULL (rule holds vacuously under 3VL, acceptable).
issues.requested_revision: No change required for 3VL; confirm in a comment that derived formulas are only asserted for non-NULL operands.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic rule for donations.donation_total gives two formulas: `donation_total = donation_to_project + donation_optional_support` and, conditionally, `donation_total = donation_to_project` when `donation_included_optional_support = 'f'`. The evidence row (20.0 + 0.75 = 20.75 but total 20.0 with included_optional_support='f') supports the conditional. The program implements both in `_derive_donations`. This is consistent, but the specification's `uncertainty` field admits the formula 'holds only when optional support is included'; the conditional is the correct reading. No blocking issue.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports fk_violations: 808 across all 20 instances (validity: invalid 20/20, reason new_integrity_failures). The writer disables FK enforcement (`con.execute('pragma foreign_keys = OFF')` in writer.py) and the generator deliberately injects ~5% orphan FK values in `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` (instance.py) for donations.projectid, resources.projectid, essays.projectid. The schema declares `foreign key (projectid) references projects(projectid)` on donations and resources, so orphan values are genuine FK violations, not merely 'unmatched join rows'.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the unmatched_join_rows rule with the declared FK constraints. Either (a) keep FK integrity by only using NULL (not orphan) values for nullable FKs, and obtain 'parent rows without children' by simply not referencing some parents, or (b) if orphan values are truly required, the specification must state that FK constraints are intentionally relaxed and the integrity checker must be told so. As written, the program produces 808 FK violations per run, which the validity check flags as blocking. The specification's generic rule ('5% NULL and 5% orphan values where nullable') conflicts with the schema's FK constraints and must be corrected.

issues.evidence: The specification's `unmatched_join_rows` generic rule says 'for each nullable FK: ~5% NULL and ~5% orphan (non-matching) values'. But donations.projectid and resources.projectid are declared with `foreign key ... references projects(projectid)`, and the integrity checker counts these as fk_violations. The specification does not acknowledge that orphan FK values violate the declared constraints, nor does it instruct the checker to tolerate them.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the specification whether orphan FK values are permitted despite declared FK constraints. If not, remove the orphan-injection requirement and rely on NULL FKs plus unreferenced parents to satisfy unmatched_join_rows. If yes, document that the integrity checker must exclude FK violations on these columns, and explain why the schema's FK declarations are treated as advisory.

issues.evidence: essays.teacher_acctid is 100% NULL in generated rows (feedback: 'essays.teacher_acctid: generated rows: NULL 4102 / 4102'). `_derive_essays` builds `pid_to_tid` from projects' projectid->teacher_acctid, but `_apply_nulls` is applied to projects.teacher_acctid (10% NULL) and, more importantly, essays.projectid is drawn from the parent pool with 5% orphan values, so orphan projectids map to None. However 100% NULL indicates the lookup is failing entirely — likely because essays.projectid values are generated as fresh hex32 (via `_HEX32` set) rather than drawn from the projects pool, so `pid_to_tid.get(pid)` returns None for every row. The dependency `essays.teacher_acctid copied from projects.teacher_acctid` is therefore not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Fix `_derive_essays` / FK handling so essays.projectid is drawn from the projects.projectid pool (as the dependency requires) and teacher_acctid is copied from the matching project. Verify that non-orphan essays rows get a non-NULL teacher_acctid matching the parent. Note: the NULL rule allows NULLs but not 100% NULL for a column that should be copied from a parent.

issues.evidence: The specification's `table_sizes_per_instance` fixes projects=200, essays=200, donations=400, resources=400. `_spec_size` varies each by ±30, but the execution feedback shows generated rows far exceeding these: projects 4184, donations 8046, resources 8130, essays 4102 across 20 instances — i.e. ~209 projects, ~402 donations, ~406 resources, ~205 essays per instance. This is roughly consistent with the spec sizes (200/400/400/200) plus the compact rows, so the per-instance sizes are approximately correct. However, the writer appends to a copy of the compact DB, so total row counts include original rows; the 'generated rows' counts in feedback (e.g. 4184/20 ≈ 209) are close to spec. This is acceptable but should be confirmed.
issues.requested_revision: No change required if per-instance generated counts are ~200/200/400/400; confirm the writer's row accounting distinguishes generated from compact rows (the summary file rows_added is empty in feedback, suggesting the sidecar summary is not being written).

issues.evidence: The CLI prints a summary but `rows_added`/`rows_skipped` are empty in the execution feedback (`"rows_added": {}, "rows_skipped": {}`). The writer returns `{'rows_ok':..., 'rows_failed':...}` but never writes the sidecar summary file that cli.py reads (`%s__%s_summary.json`). So the reported row accounting is silently empty.
issues.requested_revision: Have `write_instance_sqlite` (or the CLI) write the sidecar summary JSON with rows_added/rows_skipped so the execution feedback reflects actual insert counts. This is a reporting gap, not a correctness blocker, but it obscures whether rows were skipped.

issues.evidence: The specification lists `donations.donation_total` formula `donation_total = donation_to_project + donation_optional_support` when `donation_included_optional_support='t'`, else `= donation_to_project`. The program implements this in `_derive_donations`, but `_apply_nulls` is applied AFTER derivation and plants NULLs in donation_total (10%), donation_to_project, and donation_optional_support independently. Under 3VL this is acceptable (rule holds when not FALSE), but the specification should state that the formula is only asserted for non-NULL operands — which it does in `uncertainty`. This is consistent.

issues.evidence: `_apply_dup_share` is applied to `_DUP_SHARE` columns including `donations.donation_message`, but `donation_message` is also in `_NULL_SHARE` (0.259). `_apply_nulls` runs after `_build_column_values` (which applies dup share), so NULLs are planted after duplication — fine. However `_DUP_SHARE` includes `projects.date_posted`, `projects.grade_level`, `projects.teacher_prefix`, `resources.item_quantity`, `donations.donation_message`, `projects.school_latitude`, `projects.school_longitude`. For `date_posted` and `item_quantity`, the sampler path is the generic `else` branch (not enum), and `_apply_dup_share` is applied — consistent with spec. No issue found here.

The program's `_NEAR_VARIANTS` for essays.title includes the literals but `_near_variants` produces L, L||'x', lower(L), one-char-sub — it does NOT produce the `L||'%'` LIKE variant that the spec's near_variant rule requires ('for LIKE targets also include L||'%''). The atomic ops show a target literal 'Creating Memories and Inspiring Dreams%'.
issues.requested_revision: Add the `L||'%'` variant for LIKE targets in `_near_variants` (or a separate LIKE-variant injection) so the essays.title LIKE pattern is exercised. Currently the '%' variant is missing.

issues.evidence: `_boundary_variants` for `projects.school_city` returns [L, lower(L), upper(L)] = ['Los Angeles','los angeles','LOS ANGELES'], matching the spec's comparison_boundary targets.
